candidates.source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — dataset on IMF Data portal
candidates.why_relevant: Core supranational supply-side database for ATM and POS terminal counts, per 100,000 adults and per 1,000 km2, plus branches, deposit/loan accounts and (recent vintages) mobile-money and digital-payment series. Montenegro is a reporting jurisdiction; 2025 release covers 163 economies, 121 series, 2004-2024. This is the single best cross-country-comparable ATM/POS density series for ME.
candidates.access_status: public, free, bulk download and API (SDMX)
candidates.legal_status: IMF terms of use; redistribution with attribution generally permitted for statistical data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX/API pull of FAS dataset filtered to REF_AREA=ME on an annual cadence (release typically late October); fall back to CSV bulk download.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from IMF press releases
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey Montenegro ATMs POS per 100,000 adults data
IMF Data portal FAS dataset "data.imf.org/en/datasets" Financial Access Survey

candidates.source_name: IMF FAS annual results press release / Highlights report
candidates.why_relevant: Announces each annual FAS vintage, its coverage changes and new series (POS pilot disaggregated rural/urban, fintech lending, gender splits). Best trigger signal for a refresh of the Montenegro FAS pull and for knowing which new indicators became available.
candidates.legal_status: IMF copyright, quotable with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual check each October of the IMF news feed filtered for 'Financial Access Survey'.
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey Montenegro ATMs POS per 100,000 adults data

candidates.source_name: IMF Montenegro country page (Article IV, country reports, mission statements)
candidates.why_relevant: Hub for all IMF output on Montenegro: Article IV staff reports with banking-sector and payments annexes, selected issues papers, technical assistance reports, and the statistical appendix tables. Snowballs into individual country reports (e.g. CR 25/304, 2025 Article IV concluded November 2025).
candidates.legal_status: IMF copyright; staff reports free to read and cite
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the country page quarterly; download new Country Report PDFs and extract the statistical annex tables.
queries_used: Montenegro IMF Article IV 2025 staff report country page imf.org
MMF Crna Gora izvještaj konsultacije Član IV bankarski sektor podaci

candidates.source_name: IMF Country Report No. 25/304 — Montenegro 2025 Article IV Consultation
candidates.why_relevant: Most recent full staff report; contains banking-sector soundness tables, credit and deposit aggregates, and macro-financial context (growth 3.2% 2024/H1-2025, inflation 4.9% Sept 2025) plus EU-accession-2028 framing that drives payments-modernisation policy.
candidates.legal_status: IMF copyright, citation permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Direct PDF fetch and table extraction; re-check annually after each Article IV Board date.
queries_used: Montenegro IMF Article IV 2025 staff report country page imf.org

candidates.source_name: IMF Financial Soundness Indicators (FSI / FSIC dataset)
candidates.why_relevant: Standardised banking-sector soundness series (capital adequacy, NPLs, liquidity, profitability) reported by the Central Bank of Montenegro to the IMF; gives cross-country-comparable context for the banking market that underpins card/POS acquiring economics. Montenegro received IMF TA specifically on FSI compilation (2019 TA report).
candidates.legal_status: IMF terms of use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX pull filtered to Montenegro, quarterly cadence.
queries_used: IMF Financial Soundness Indicators Montenegro data.imf.org dataset

candidates.source_name: IMF Data portal (data.imf.org) — general dataset catalogue (IFS, MFS, BOP)
candidates.why_relevant: Umbrella catalogue for all IMF statistical datasets in which Montenegro appears (International Financial Statistics, Monetary and Financial Statistics, Balance of Payments incl. remittance/travel credits). Portal was re-platformed, so old ?sk= query-string links coexist with new /en/datasets/ paths — worth mapping once.
candidates.legal_status: IMF terms of use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off crawl of the dataset catalogue to build a stable ME series map, then scheduled SDMX pulls.
queries_used: IMF Data portal FAS dataset "data.imf.org/en/datasets" Financial Access Survey

candidates.source_name: World Bank Global Findex Database 2025
candidates.why_relevant: Demand-side benchmark: account ownership, card ownership and use, made/received digital payments, mobile phone and internet access, financial resilience. 2025 edition surveyed ~145,000 adults in 141 economies with ~300 indicators; Montenegro is in the country set (see microdata catalogue listing of 140 economies).
candidates.access_status: public; report PDF, country dashboards and downloadable indicator files
candidates.legal_status: CC BY licence typical for World Bank data/publications
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the Findex indicator file (download-data page) and filter to Montenegro; triennial refresh (2011/2014/2017/2021/2025).
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball to microdata catalogue
queries_used: World Bank Global Findex 2025 Montenegro account ownership digital payments

candidates.source_name: World Bank Microdata Library — Global Findex collection (respondent-level microdata)
candidates.why_relevant: Respondent-level Findex files allow custom Montenegro cuts (age, income quintile, urban/rural, gender) that the headline indicators do not publish — e.g. card-payment use among older or rural adults, a key segmentation input for POS/ATM strategy.
candidates.access_status: registration/licensed download for microdata; catalogue metadata public
candidates.legal_status: Microdata licence terms; check redistribution restrictions before republishing
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Register, request the 2025 Findex dataset, extract the ME subsample; do not redistribute raw microdata.
queries_used: World Bank Global Findex 2025 Montenegro account ownership digital payments

candidates.source_name: World Bank Open Data — Montenegro indicator pages (WDI / GFDD)
candidates.why_relevant: Re-publishes IMF FAS-derived indicators (ATMs per 100,000 adults, commercial bank branches) and World Development Indicators / Global Financial Development Database series for Montenegro in a convenient API. Useful as an easy time-series backbone, but it is a downstream copy of IMF FAS — treat FAS as the primary.
candidates.legal_status: CC BY 4.0 for most World Bank datasets
candidates.suggested_collection_method: World Bank indicator API: /v2/country/MNE/indicator/FB.ATM.TOTL.P5 etc., annual refresh.

candidates.source_name: World Bank Data360 — hosted IMF FAS and partner datasets
candidates.why_relevant: New World Bank cross-agency data platform that re-hosts IMF FAS and many other partner datasets with a unified API; often easier to query than the IMF portal and useful as a redundancy path when data.imf.org changes URL structure.
candidates.legal_status: Terms follow the original data provider's licence
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Data360 API pull with REF_AREA=MNE as a fallback/cross-check against the IMF source.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from FAS dataset search results

candidates.source_name: World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (GPSS)
candidates.why_relevant: Central-bank questionnaire covering payment-system infrastructure, retail instruments, oversight, interoperability and national payment strategies for 100+ jurisdictions (6th round released Oct 2023). If Montenegro's CBCG responded, this is one of the few standardised international views of ME payment-system architecture.
candidates.access_status: public data catalogue entry; dataset download
candidates.legal_status: World Bank data catalogue licence, typically CC BY
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the GPSS dataset and check whether Montenegro is among respondents; roughly every 3-4 years.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles category inference (who aggregates payment-system data?)

candidates.source_name: Remittance Prices Worldwide (World Bank)
candidates.why_relevant: Corridor-level cost of sending money, covering 377 corridors from 48 sending to 111 receiving countries. Relevant to Montenegro as a remittance-receiving economy (remittance inflows ~12.6% of GDP in 2020 per WB-derived series) and to cash-out/ATM demand. Montenegro's presence as a receiving corridor must be verified in the DataBank tables.
candidates.legal_status: World Bank licence, attribution

candidates.why_relevant: Annual/semi-annual remittance inflow and outflow estimates by country plus bilateral remittance matrices; standard supranational source for Montenegro remittance volumes. Note KNOMAD's hosting arrangement ran 2013-2024, so continuity of the series under a new home should be checked.
candidates.legal_status: World Bank licence, attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch each new Migration and Development Brief PDF plus its Excel annex; extract the Montenegro row.

candidates.source_name: Eurostat ICT usage in households and by individuals (isoc_i) — Montenegro national metadata + databrowser
candidates.why_relevant: The isoc_i family is the EU-harmonised source for internet-banking usage, e-commerce and online-payment behaviour. Montenegro has run the survey since 2011 and transmits microdata to Eurostat, so ME appears alongside EU averages — the best comparable demand-side digital-payments proxy between Findex waves. The '_me' country-specific metadata file confirms ME reporting.
candidates.access_status: public databrowser + API; microdata by research application
candidates.legal_status: Eurostat re-use with attribution; microdata under research-access contract

candidates.source_name: ECB — Western Balkans / candidate-country central banking cooperation and euroisation research
candidates.why_relevant: The ECB runs an EU-funded technical cooperation programme with the Central Bank of Montenegro on ESCB-standard alignment (including statistics), and publishes Occasional Papers assessing financial stability and euroisation in candidate countries. Montenegro is unilaterally euroised, which shapes cash-usage dynamics; note the ECB explicitly does NOT collect euro-substitution data for countries where the euro is legal tender (Montenegro, Kosovo).
candidates.legal_status: ECB copyright, citation permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the ECB publications feed and press releases for 'Montenegro' / 'Western Balkans' / 'candidate countries'; harvest Occasional Papers.

negative_findings.description: BIS CPMI Red Book payments statistics do not cover Montenegro. Searches of the CPMI member/jurisdiction lists (27 member jurisdictions, expanded in 2018 to add Argentina, Indonesia, Spain) returned no Montenegro entry.
negative_findings.result_summary: Montenegro is not a CPMI member jurisdiction; no ME series should be expected in the Red Book / data.bis.org CPMI topic datasets. BIS remains valuable only as a definitional standard and comparator set.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort and stops a false assumption in the run scope that BIS is a Montenegro data source.

negative_findings.description: ECB does not collect euro-substitution / euroisation survey data for Montenegro because the euro is legal tender there (same for Kosovo). ECB euro-substitution ratios exist for North Macedonia and Serbia but not ME.
negative_findings.result_summary: No ECB euro-cash-substitution series for Montenegro; ECB coverage of ME is qualitative (cooperation programme, occasional papers), not a statistical series.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cash-usage analysis for Montenegro cannot lean on ECB euroisation statistics and must come from CBCG or IMF FAS-type indicators instead.

negative_findings.description: IMF FAS POS-terminal series for Montenegro was not directly confirmed in the search layer; FAS documentation describes POS terminals as introduced via a pilot study with rural/urban disaggregation, and ATM-per-100k values for ME were visible, but the POS-per-100k ME series itself was not observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: ATM density for ME appears present in FAS/WDI; POS density presence in FAS for ME is a hypothesis requiring a direct dataset query.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: POS density is a core deliverable of this cell; the collection pass must explicitly test for the ME POS series rather than assume it.

negative_findings.description: Whether the Central Bank of Montenegro responded to the World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (6th round, Oct 2023) was not established from search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: GPSS is a strong candidate but ME participation is unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If CBCG did not respond, GPSS yields nothing for ME and priority should drop.

negative_findings.description: Local-language (sr/me/bs) searching surfaced very little supranational statistical material: IMF publishes some country reports in Bosnian/Serbian (e.g. the Bosnian-language BiH country report and older Bosnian Article IV translations), but no Montenegro-specific IMF/World Bank/Eurostat statistical dataset in Montenegrin was found. Local-language coverage is dominated by media reporting (Dan, MINA, Investitor, Bankar.me) and by CBCG/MONSTAT pages describing the relationship rather than by the supranational data itself.
negative_findings.result_summary: Supranational statistical databases covering ME are effectively English-only; local-language value is limited to intermediary/commentary layers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations: the sr-language search budget for this cell is better spent on national publishers (cell scope elsewhere) than on chasing translated international datasets.

negative_findings.description: IMF's data portal has been re-platformed: legacy links use query strings (data.imf.org/?sk=E5DCAB7E-...) while newer links use path form (data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.STA:FAS). Both forms appear live in search results; neither was fetch-verified in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: URL form for IMF datasets is in flux; the deterministic verification pass should test both forms.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hard-coding a single IMF URL form risks silent collection failure.

coverage_gaps.description: No supranational source found that publishes Montenegro card-scheme-level statistics (cards issued by scheme, transaction volumes/values, e-money) in a standardised cross-country form — the BIS Red Book, which would normally carry this, excludes ME.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route card/transaction statistics to national publishers (CBCG payment statistics) and to scheme/industry sources; use FAS and Findex only for access and usage proxies.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional development banks and other supranationals that may compile ME banking/payments data — EBRD (Transition Report, Banking Environment and Performance Survey), EIB (CESEE Bank Lending Survey), Vienna Initiative, EFSE, OECD, UNCTAD — were not searched within this cell's budget.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up sweep on EBRD/EIB/OECD/Vienna Initiative for Montenegro banking and payments indicators; EIB CESEE Bank Lending Survey and EBRD BEPS are the highest-likelihood hits.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice was fetch-verified; all entries rest on search-result evidence. Several specific dataset paths (IMF FSIC, IMF FAS path form, Data360 IMF_FAS, KNOMAD landing page) are plausible-but-unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic liveness pass resolve all URLs; treat 403/timeout as bot-defence rather than death, and re-derive 404s from the parent portal's catalogue.

coverage_gaps.description: Supranational sources give Montenegro only national-level annual figures; no sub-national (coastal vs northern municipalities) ATM/POS density is available internationally, despite FAS piloting rural/urban POS disaggregation.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check whether Montenegro participates in the FAS rural/urban POS pilot; otherwise sub-national granularity must come from national or commercial sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin/Serbian-language access points to supranational data (translated IMF country reports for ME, MONSTAT's Eurostat-facing pages, CBCG statistics in local language) were only lightly mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do a dedicated sr-language sweep of imf.org translated publications for Crna Gora and of monstat.org Eurostat-transmission pages to build the local terminology map.

coverage_gaps.description: Eurostat's Montenegro coverage is uneven: reporting indicates GDP and inflation available for 2025 while unemployment and net FDI series end around 2020, reflecting MONSTAT capacity constraints (operating at ~56% of planned staff).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before relying on any Eurostat ME series, check its last available period per table code; prefer IMF FAS/Findex where Eurostat lags.

brief: Montenegro's supranational statistical footprint is concentrated in three families: the IMF (Financial Access Survey for ATM/POS and account-access density, Financial Soundness Indicators for banking-sector health, and Article IV country reports such as CR 25/304 for narrative and annex tables), the World Bank group (Global Findex 2025 for demand-side card and digital-payment behaviour, its microdata for custom cuts, WDI/GFDD and Data360 re-hosts, plus remittance datasets), and the EU statistical system (Eurostat enlargement and ICT-usage series, where Montenegro reports via MONSTAT under IPA alignment and internet-banking/e-commerce indicators are the best between-Findex proxy). Two expected sources are effectively absent: BIS CPMI Red Book excludes Montenegro because it is not a CPMI member, and the ECB does not compile euro-substitution statistics for a country where the euro is already legal tender, leaving the ECB relevant only through its CBCG cooperation programme and occasional papers. Practical consequences for collection: card-scheme-level transaction statistics have no supranational home for ME and must come from national publishers; the FAS POS-per-100k series for Montenegro is a hypothesis to be tested directly rather than assumed; and local-language material on these bodies is commentary and relationship description, not the data itself, so sr-language effort in this cell should be minimal. Third-party mirrors (DBnomics, FRED) are worth wiring in as redundancy and revision-detection given the IMF data portal's ongoing URL re-platforming.
